problem: Map the CLI as an audit event source and consumer for a comprehensive enterprise audit trail system.

files.why: Central HTTP layer (hxFetch). All CLI-to-server communication flows through here. Retry logic (3 attempts), 30s timeout, Bearer/API-key auth. Audit events from CLI would be captured server-side via these API calls.
Credential management: multi-org config in ~/.hlx/config.json. Stores API keys, server URLs, current org. Relevant for audit identity (which CLI user/key performed actions).
CLI entry point routing to 9 command modules. Maps the full CLI surface area for audit coverage.
Inspection commands (repos, db, logs, api). The inspect module is already audit-logged server-side via InspectionAuditLog.
Ticket commands: create, rerun, continue, list, artifacts. These generate auditable server-side events.
Goal commands: create, terminate, resume. State transition commands that should be audit-logged.

facts: CLI version 1.3.4 (hlx binary). Node-based, distributed via GitHub releases.
9 command modules: tickets, goals, comments, inspect, library, org, token, login, skill, preview, update.
No client-side audit logging. All operations are API calls to helix-global-server.
Inspect commands are already audit-logged server-side via InspectionAuditLog (6,516 records in production).
CLI uses X-Helix-Org-ID header for org-scoped requests — audit identity is available server-side.
Env var overrides: HELIX_API_KEY, HELIX_URL, HELIX_INSPECT_TOKEN — relevant for audit identity source.
unknowns: Should the CLI have a local audit log command to view audit events for the current org?
Are CLI operations distinguishable from UI operations in server-side audit logs? (User-Agent header could differentiate.)
